questions.question: When using ABS brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake pedal harder than normal.
Press the brake pedal the same way you normally would.
Press the brake pedal more lightly than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brake pedal the same way you normally would.
questions.explanation: With ABS brakes, use your brakes normally. Do not change how you brake just because the vehicle has ABS.

questions.question: What does a shut-off valve do?

options.text: Is located on the front of a trailer.
Is located on the instrument panel.
Stops air from leaving the air brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from leaving the air brake system.
questions.explanation: A shut-off valve controls air flow between trailers. The rear shut-off valve must stay closed to prevent air from leaving the braking system.

questions.question: If your trailer's spring brakes do not release when you press the air supply control, what should you do?

options.text: Check that the air line connections are tight and connected.
Turn on the Anti-Lock Braking System.
Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the air line connections are tight and connected.
questions.explanation: Before driving, make sure all equipment works properly. If the trailer brakes do not release, check that all air line connections are properly connected and sealed.

questions.question: Where should cargo be placed to help prevent a rollover?

options.text: As high as possible inside the trailer.
As low as possible inside the trailer.
On the passenger side of the trailer.
On the driver's side of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible inside the trailer.
questions.explanation: Keep cargo weight low to the ground to reduce rollover risk. Do not put weight on just one side of the trailer, as this can cause leaning and increase the risk of a rollover.

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combination vehicles are most at risk for rollovers from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: When should the air supply control lever be in its "normal" position?

options.text: When using the trailer emergency brakes.

questions.explanation: Older vehicles use levers instead of knobs for tractor protection controls. The air supply control should be in its "normal" position when you are pulling a trailer.

questions.question: Why is proper coupling technique important?

options.text: It is the same on all vehicles.
It is needed for safe vehicle operation.
It includes not greasing the fifth wheel plate.
It can be learned over time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is needed for safe vehicle operation.
questions.explanation: Knowing how to couple and uncouple correctly is very important for safe operation. Improper coupling is dangerous.

questions.question: What is one function of the emergency air line?

options.text: Flash when air pressure is too low.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line (also called the supply line) has two jobs. It supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: When uncoupling a trailer, what position should the landing gear be in?
questions.explanation: Before driving, landing gear must be fully raised. When uncoupling, lower the landing gear until it is firmly on the ground. If the trailer is loaded, lower the gear and turn the crank a few more times to take some weight off the trailer.

questions.question: If you are backing and are not sure about your path, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and get out to look.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and get out to look.
questions.explanation: If you are unsure about your path while backing, stop the vehicle and get out to check your path before continuing.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side on a curved path. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate.
The service air line will activate.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If it loses pressure, the emergency trailer brakes will activate automatically.

questions.question: If you need to back your trailer but cannot back in a straight line, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side on a curved path. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: How should you brake when driving a trailer with ABS?

options.text: Do not press the brakes as hard as you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Use extra braking force to activate the ABS.
Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
Try to brake less often than you would in a vehicle without ABS.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake the same way you would in a vehicle without ABS.
questions.explanation: Brake the same way with ABS as you would without it. Do not change your braking habits.

questions.question: What happens when a trailer's wheels lock up?

options.text: The trailer tends to swing around.
The cab will swing, but the trailer will stay straight.
The tires will likely go flat.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer tends to swing around.
questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is even more likely if the trailer is lightly loaded.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves and listen for air escaping. This checks that air reaches all brakes. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers turn or change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: When do large combination vehicles take the longest time to stop?
questions.explanation: Empty vehicles take longer to stop than loaded ones. With less weight, the wheels have less grip on the road.

questions.question: Are combination vehicles harder to drive than single commercial vehicles?

options.text: No, they are easier to drive.
Yes, they are more difficult to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are more difficult to drive.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are harder to drive. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over than single commercial vehicles.

questions.question: If your trailer begins to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly turn the steering wheel one way, then the other.

questions.explanation: Release the brakes to help the wheels grip the road again. Once traction returns, the trailer will straighten out and follow the tractor.
